title: Charvaka and the Heterodox Traditions: Philosophy Without God or Soul

questions.question: The astika/nastika divide in Indian philosophy is fundamentally about:
options: Acceptance or rejection of the Vedas as a valid source of knowledge
questions.rationale: Astika means accepting the Vedas as pramana (valid knowledge), not belief in God — Samkhya is astika yet posits no creator.

questions.question: Charvaka accepts which pramana as the only valid source of knowledge?
questions.rationale: Charvaka's severe empiricism accepts only direct perception, rejecting inference and testimony as unperceived or second-hand.

questions.question: Why does Charvaka reject inference?
options: Because the universal connection (vyapti) between things can never be perceived across all cases
Because inference only works in mathematics
questions.rationale: To infer fire from smoke requires knowing the two are always concomitant — and no one can survey all cases past and future, so inference presupposes what it should prove.

questions.question: According to Charvaka, how many elements constitute reality?
options: Four: earth, water, fire, and air
questions.rationale: Charvaka holds that only the four mahabhutas — earth, water, fire, and air — exist; consciousness arises from their combination, as fermentation arises from grain.

questions.question: Ajita Kesakambalin, Charvaka's first historical teacher, is known to us mainly from:
options: The Buddhist Samannaphala Sutta's list of six heterodox teachers
questions.rationale: Ajita Kesakambalin appears in the Buddhist Samannaphala Sutta as one of the six heterodox teachers contemporary with the Buddha; almost no Charvaka texts survive.

questions.question: The Ajivika school taught which core doctrine?
options: Hedonism — pleasure is the only good
questions.rationale: Makkhali Gosala's Ajivikas held that niyati (fate) governs everything: effort is powerless, and every soul traverses a fixed series of lives before automatic liberation.

questions.question: Who is traditionally credited as the founder of the Charvaka system, and which 14th-century compendium preserves its doctrines?
questions.rationale: Charvaka is attributed to the legendary Brihaspati, and survives mainly through opponents — above all Madhavacharya's Sarvadarshanasamgraha (14th century).

questions.question: A paradox of Ajivika practice was that its members:
options: Practised severe austerities despite believing effort cannot change fate
questions.rationale: The Ajivikas practised nakedness, fasting, and harsh penance — not to burn away karma, but as the destiny-appointed path fixed by niyati.

questions.question: Which school is astika despite positing no creator God?
questions.rationale: Astika concerns acceptance of Vedic authority, not theism — Samkhya accepts the Vedas yet explains the world through purusha and prakriti without a creator.

questions.question: On Charvaka's view, consciousness is:
options: An eternal soul distinct from the body
A by-product of the combination of the four elements
questions.rationale: As the Sarvadarshanasamgraha reports: just as betel, areca, and lime combine to yield red colour, so the elements combine to produce consciousness — which ends at death.
